page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AWS Graviton processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv8 64-bit architecture running at 2.6 GHz, with a single thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and includes 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps under the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results place the c7gd.2xlarge in the average performance tier for most compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1532.19, and the multi-core score is 12241.51. Memory bandwidth is measured at 775.35 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 148.04 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In application-specific tests, the instance achieves a static web serving throughput of 15.36 GB/sec and handles 12.54 million Redis SET operations per second. However, cryptography and encryption benchmarks show weaker relative performance, with a PassMark CPU encryption score of 1110.82.

The ARM-based architecture of the Graviton processor offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not require x86-specific instruction sets. The inclusion of 474 GB of local NVMe SSD storage makes this instance highly suitable for applications requiring fast scratch space or local caching. Recommended workloads include distributed data processing, static web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. It is less suited for large-scale language model inference, as demonstrated by poor prompt processing speeds on 7B models.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gd.2xlarge is an ARM64 compute-optimized instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps managed by the Nitro hypervisor. Benchmarks indicate average performance across standard compute and memory tasks, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12241.51 and a static web serving throughput of 15.36 GB/sec. However, cryptography and encryption tests show weaker results. The combination of dedicated ARM cores and fast local NVMe storage provides qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense workloads. This server is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression, though it is not recommended for heavy machine learning inference workloads.
